transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I really appreciate it, and I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. Um, well, I guess I'm here just to... just to check on a little issue I've been having at work. It's probably nothing too major, but I want to make sure I'm doing the right thing by being here. 

I'm a retail supervisor, and lately, when I try to explain things to my team—like the inventory numbers, or just going over the weekend schedule—my words kind of... well, they start jumping around a bit. I'll be talking about the delivery trucks, and then suddenly I'm on about Thursdays, and then the church grill, and... and maybe my boss's tone of voice. 

I try really hard to be clear and professional, I really do, but people just look at me like they can't follow what I'm saying at all. It's quite embarrassing, to be honest with you. Am I explaining that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
When you're having these moments where your thoughts seem to jump around, do you ever hear voices or see things that other people don't seem to notice?

Oh, goodness, no. No, doctor, nothing like that. I—I'm sorry if I made it sound much worse than it actually is. It's really just my words getting a bit... tangled up when I'm speaking to the staff. 

I definitely don't hear anyone talking when they aren't there, or see anything unusual. I just... my mind just races ahead of my mouth, I suppose. I hope that's a good sign? I want to be completely honest and helpful for you, of course, but I haven't noticed anything like voices or visions at all. Is that the sort of information you needed? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
When you write things down—like emails or reports at work—do you have the same problem with your words jumping around, or does that come out more organized on paper?

Well, um... writing things down, like emails and such? Actually, I think... I think I do much better with that. Yes, definitely better. I always try to be very careful with my reports. 

When I'm typing, I have a moment to—to look at the words before I send them off, you know? I can backspace if something doesn't look quite right. I mean, maybe sometimes an email gets a little... lengthy, or I might add a small detail about the store layout that wasn't strictly necessary, but I really do try to keep it professional. I haven't had anyone complain about my emails, at least not that they've told me. 

Does that make sense? I hope that's helpful. I just want to assure you that I'm still managing my duties as best I can. Is that... is that the kind of detail you were looking for?

How long have you been experiencing this difficulty with your words jumping around when you speak? Has this been something you've noticed your whole life, or is it something that started more recently?

Oh, definitely not my whole life, doctor. No, no, I've actually always prided myself on being quite a good communicator. 

Um... I suppose it's really just been more recent. I'd say... maybe about six months now? Give or take a little. It's just been the last half year or so that these, well, these jumbled explanations started happening out on the sales floor. And sometimes I might just have these odd little stops where I pause for a moment in the middle of a sentence. 

But it hasn't been forever, I promise. Just about six months. I hope that doesn't sound too terribly concerning? I really am trying my absolute best to manage it at work, and I don't want you to think my whole career has been like this. Is six months... is that the kind of timeline you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to know.
Over these past six months while you've been having trouble with your words jumping around, how has your mood been? Have you been feeling sad, down, or hopeless at all?

Oh, no, no, doctor. I wouldn't say I've been feeling hopeless at all. I mean, everyone has a slightly off day here and there, don't they? But overall, my mood has been quite fine. I try to stay very positive, especially at work—it's important to keep a good attitude for the team, you know? 

I certainly haven't been sitting around feeling sad or down. I've been keeping up with my routines and trying to be as productive as always. I really don't want to give you the impression that I'm depressed or anything like that. I'm just a bit... frustrated with my words sometimes, that's all. 

Does that answer your question properly? I hope it's a good sign that my mood has stayed upbeat despite the little speaking hiccups. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Over these past six months, have you noticed any change in how much you enjoy the things you usually like to do—whether that's hobbies, time with friends or family, or activities outside of work?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all. I still very much enjoy my downtime. When I'm not managing the store, I... well, I have my little projects around the house, and I always look forward to seeing my family on the weekends. 

I try to stay very active and engaged, you know? It's important to have a good balance, so I make sure to keep up with the things I love doing. I certainly haven't stopped liking my hobbies or anything like that. I'm still the same old me in that regard, just plugging along and enjoying my evenings. 

Is that... does that sound alright to you? I hope that shows I'm keeping a healthy routine outside of work. I really am trying to do everything I'm supposed to.

When your words are jumping around at work, do you find yourself repeating sounds or syllables, like 'b-b-but' or 'the the the,' or do you sometimes get stuck on a word and have trouble getting it out?

Oh, no, no, doctor. It's not like that at all. I don't... I don't stutter, if that's what you mean. I've never had a problem like that. 

It's more just... well, the ideas get a bit jumbled, or I might just stop for a second, like I mentioned. But I'm definitely not repeating sounds or getting stuck on a single word like 'b-b-but.' I'm very careful about how I present myself on the floor, and I think a stutter would be... well, it wouldn't be very professional, would it? 

I really don't want you to think I'm struggling that badly. It's just a little mix-up with the sentences sometimes. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it clearly enough for you. I just want to be sure you have the right picture of what's going on.

When you're talking to your team and your words jump around, would you say it's because you're thinking faster than you can speak, or is it more that you're having trouble organizing your thoughts about what you want to say in the first place?

Well, I wouldn't say I have trouble organizing my thoughts. I mean, I'm a manager, so I'm very organized, naturally. It's just... I think maybe I just have a lot going on in my head all at once. 

When I try to explain things to the team, like the inventory numbers or the weekend schedule, I just... well, my mind is so active, you know? The words just start jumping. Like, I'll be talking about the delivery trucks, and then suddenly I'm mentioning Thursdays, and then I might bring up the church grill, and then maybe something about my boss's tone of voice. It all connects in my head, I promise you. 

But sometimes people just... they look at me like they can't quite follow what I'm saying. I think maybe I just speak a little too passionately sometimes, or I'm trying to cover too much ground at once. I'm definitely not disorganized, though. I hope you can see that. I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job and covering all the bases. Is it normal to just have a lot of thoughts connecting like that?

When you're about to explain something complicated to your team, like the inventory system, do you usually have a clear plan in your head about what you want to say before you start talking, or do you find yourself figuring out what to say as you go along?

Oh, well, I always have a plan. I'm very prepared, doctor. I wouldn't just go into a meeting without knowing what I'm going to say. That wouldn't be very professional, right? 

I usually have a very clear idea of the main points I need to cover, especially with something important like inventory. It's just... well, like I said, sometimes when I'm actually speaking, all those other connected thoughts just sort of... come up. But the plan is definitely there to begin with. I always make sure I'm prepared. 

I hope that shows I'm taking my responsibilities seriously. It's important to me that you know I'm trying to do things the right way. Does that sound like a good approach to you?

When you're in the middle of explaining something and your words jump around, do you ever find yourself unable to think of the right word to use, or do you always know what word you want to say but just end up saying something different instead?

Oh, no, it's nothing like that. I don't... I don't forget my words. My vocabulary is actually quite strong. I have my bachelor's degree, you know, so I'm very capable of finding the right word. 

And I definitely don't just blurt out the wrong thing instead. That would make me look a bit foolish in front of my team, wouldn't it? I always know exactly what word I want to use. It's really just... well, just the thoughts moving a bit fast and connecting, like we talked about. 

I hope you don't think my memory is slipping or anything. I'm still very sharp, I promise you. I wouldn't want you to get the impression that I'm losing my grip on my vocabulary. Does that help clear things up? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need to know.
When you're speaking to your team and your words jump around, would you say you're talking very quickly, or is your speed of talking about normal?

I don't think I talk too fast. I mean, my speed is pretty normal, I'd say. I'm not rushing through things or trying to speed-talk. I want my team to understand me, so I try to keep a very reasonable, professional pace. 

Sometimes, because there's just so much energy behind what I'm saying, it might feel a little lively, but I wouldn't call it fast. I'm just trying to be thorough and engaging, you know? I hope that doesn't make it sound like I'm out of control when I speak. I really do try to keep everything at a very normal, steady speed. Is that the kind of thing you're looking to find out? I just want to be sure I'm answering correctly.

When you're talking to your team and those thoughts jump around, do you ever make any unusual sounds or noises with your voice—like clicking, humming, or repeating little sounds—or is it purely that your sentences don't connect the way you want them to?

Oh, goodness, no. I definitely don't do anything like that. No clicking or... or humming, or repeating little sounds. That would be highly unprofessional, wouldn't it? Especially in a staff meeting or out on the sales floor. I wouldn't want anyone to think I was... well, acting strangely or anything. 

It's really just what you said—purely that the sentences don't always connect perfectly because of all those thoughts coming together. But my voice and everything else is perfectly normal. 

I always try to present myself well to my team. I hope my answers are giving you the right picture? I really don't want to give you the wrong impression about how I conduct myself at work. I'm doing my best to be helpful and give you exactly what you need.

When you were in school as a child, did your teachers or parents ever mention any concerns about how you spoke or expressed yourself, or did you have any difficulties with reading or writing back then?

Oh, no, nothing like that at all. I was a very good student, actually. My teachers always had lovely things to say about me. I didn't have any trouble reading or writing... I mean, I've always enjoyed learning, and I got my bachelor's degree, so I think I did quite well for myself. 

My parents never had to worry about how I spoke or anything. I was always very polite and articulate, even as a boy. I wouldn't want you to think I had some sort of... learning problem or anything growing up. I was quite normal, I promise. I hope that's alright? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information, doctor. I wouldn't want to mislead you about my childhood.
